Measures are being taken by the Applicant in the Bad Creek and West Bad Creek drainage basins to control erosion resulting from initial exploratory excavations and disruptions at the upper reservoir site. These measures include gates to keep out vehicle traffic and silt fences, "Hold-Gro" erosion control fabric, and planting of fast-growing ground covers (Figures 4-1 thru 4-4). Continual maintenance efforts would be necessary to ensure the success of the measures taken.
Applicant has developed an erosion and sediment pollution control plan to be implemented during construction of the project (Appendix B) to protect the Howard Creek drainage, the Whitewater River, and the Whitewater arm of Lake Jocassee. Control measures would be taken to reduce erosion from construction of project facilities and appurtenant structures. The plan includes measures to control erosion and siltation into the Whitewater River basin should the supplemental borrow area shown in Figure 1-4 be required. The plan also includes post-construction measures, including grading, planting of ground covers, and closing of roads no longer in use.
Retaining walls and cofferdams would be constructed to control runoff and siltation during construction of the tunnel adits, excavation of the power tunnel and powerhouse chamber, and construction of the underground facilities.
Sediment traps would be placed in the old stream beds in the upper reservoir area during land clearing operations and dam construction, to help contain suspended solids within the project area. Additionally, the diversion intake structure would create a settling basin behind the main dam. Water breaks and soil catchment basins would also be used to control runoff. If needed, a major settlement basin would be placed in Bad Creek, downstream from the dam site, to further minimize siltation and turbidity in Howard Creek. The scheduling and conduct of the reservoir clearing would also minimize siltation in Howard Creek. The flow of West Bad Creek would be diverted to Bad Creek before the initiation of clearing in the West Bad Creek basin. Riprap material would be placed on both faces of the dams and dike to control erosion.
